name: a dot-matrix percentage proves the ratio
looks: A big statistic builds from small square dots arranged into digit shapes, a short caption naming what it measures underneath, and a thin horizontal bar beneath that splits into two portions showing the same ratio as a share. A moment later the whole stat scatters back apart into loose drifting dots.
build: Canvas: one dot per unit sampled into the digit shapes with a tiny per-dot jitter so it never reads as a raster grid; a horizontal bar fills to the stat's value with a labelled remainder portion; on the beat's end the dots release from their grid positions and relax into a soft scatter.
sound: A soft granular patter while the dots settle into digits, a tick on the digit build, a quiet dissolve as they scatter apart.
prompt: Build a big percentage or ratio statistic out of a population of small dots rather than solid type, with a thin bar beneath splitting the same ratio into a share, then let the whole stat release back into a loose drift of dots as the beat ends -- the number should feel made of many small units, not just typeset.
